units: feet, seconds; speeds in ft/s (1 mph = 1.4667 ft/s)

references.title: NHL EDGE Pro Reference Benchmarks
references.usedFor: 22 mph burst threshold, 100 mph hard-shot threshold, top recorded speeds

references.title: NHL EDGE Skating Stats Deep Dive 2025-26
references.usedFor: league-average top speed ~21.7 mph, distance per game

topSpeed.note: 27 to 33 ft/s = 18.4 to 22.5 mph; league-average top speed in simulated games is ~21.7 mph

effort.desc: share of top speed when not chasing, rushing or far from the spot. In our own zone a defender more than defendOwnZoneUrgentBeyondFt from his spot (his man, the slot attacker he picked up, the net-front man he boxes out) skates at full effort, including while the attackers are passing.

fatigue.desc: Shift fatigue. After startsAt seconds on the ice a skater loses top speed, acceleration and hands, reaching the full penalty at fullAt seconds. A unit stuck defending past 30-45 s is the case this models.

pass.interceptNote: A defender whose stick reaches a fast pass controls it with probability interceptControlPerSkill times his skill. Otherwise, with probability deflectOnTouch, he knocks it off line: up to deflectAngleRad off its path at deflectSpeedMin to deflectSpeedMax of its speed, and it becomes a loose puck. Before sim 0.35 an uncontrolled touch left the pass untouched. Separately, every defender a pass goes by within stickReachFt gets one chance to get a stick on it, stickDeflectBase plus stickDeflectPerDef times his defense rating, and a stick on it knocks it off line the same way.

want.desc: When a carrier without a clear shot looks for a pass: always when a defender is within pressureFt plus pressurePerAggressionFt times his team's aggression, otherwise at ratePerSec (powerPlayRatePerSec on the power play) times 0.5 plus his passing rating. The pass itself still needs a clear lane and a teammate worth passing to.

pass.inFlightNote: A pass counts as on its way to the receiver, with both teams keeping their structure and the defense playing the receiver, only while it moves faster than inFlightMinFtPerSec. Slower than that it has died: it is a loose puck and both teams go for it. Before sim 0.46 a pass that stopped short stayed in flight forever, and a pass that died just short of the far blue line froze play for up to a period (the receiver was held onside and nobody else chased it).
pass.controlNote: In the offensive zone a receiver needs controlSec with the puck before he makes a discretionary pass (the expected-goal pass and the open-man pass); shots and the stuck-play passes are not held back. Without it the attacking team moved the puck several times a second. It does not apply in the other zones, where a defenseman who cannot move the puck clears it.

slap.usedWhen: defenseman or 45+ ft from the net

aim.desc: Whether a shot is on net comes from the league: the share of unblocked shots in its danger tier that hit the net in 2025-26 (in the expected-goal model's file, about 63% low, 69% medium, 78% high). A shot on net is aimed anywhere inside the posts but insidePostFt; a miss goes wide of one post by wideMinFt to wideMaxFt. Until sim 0.60 accuracy came from an aiming error that grew with distance, so close shots almost never missed and point shots mostly did.

shot.note: wrist 58 to 85 mph, slap 80 to 100 mph

xg.desc: Context flags for the expected-goal model, matching MoneyPuck's definitions: a rebound is a shot within reboundWithinSec of the goalie's last save; a rush shot comes within rushWithinSec of the team's entry into the offensive zone.

puck.note: a 75 ft/s pass glides about 180 ft; a hard rim (70+ ft/s) keeps 88 percent of its speed off the boards so a dump wraps behind the net

freeze.desc: After a save the goalie covers the puck for a faceoff when an attacker is close enough to jam a rebound; otherwise he plays it or leaves a rebound.

goalie.tierGoalScaleNote: Multiplies the shot's expected goals (divided by the league on-net share) to get the goal probability against a league-average goalie. 0.98 lands goals per game at the league rate at the NHL-average settings (the two teams' average). It was 0.72 before sim 0.35, 0.39 from 0.35 to 0.56, 0.57 in 0.57, 0.68 in 0.58, 0.74 in 0.59, 0.92 in 0.60, 1.05 in 0.61 and 1.02 in 0.62 to 0.70: since 0.35 carriers shoot whenever the expected-goal model says the look is worth it, and the sim creates more expected goals than the league (too many medium-danger looks), so the scale came down; until 0.57 it was also absorbing about three goals in ten that went in with no save roll at all; and in 0.58 man-on-man coverage started playing the puck carrier from the inside, which cut Boston's expected goals against Montreal by about a quarter, and in 0.59 zone coverage did the same, which cut Montreal's against Boston by about a sixth. In 0.60 it rose to 0.92 when shots started hitting the net at the league's rate for their danger tier: before, close shots almost never missed, so dividing by the league's 65% on-net share had been giving close chances about 1.4 times their goal rate. Above 0.72 now: both clubs' goalies are better than the league (each allowed about 10% fewer goals than expected in 2025-26), which the old accuracy hid; in 0.61 man coverage sagged more toward the net and the chance count fell again, so the scale passed 1. In 0.71 attackers stopped standing in the crease and on the goalie (physics crease): fewer tap-ins for Boston, a few more chances for Montreal, goals up about 4%, so it came back below 1. Until coverage closes the rest of the chance gap, this scale keeps scores realistic; expected goals in the reports stay unscaled so the gap stays visible.

shootout.desc: After a scoreless overtime: three shooters each, then sudden death. A shooter's chance is leagueRate scaled by his shooting rating and the goalie's high-danger save rate against the league's.

shotDecision.desc: When a carrier shoots. In the offensive zone the expected-goal model decides between shooting and passing (xgChoice); on top of that, the perimeter, probabilistic and point-shot rules throw pucks at the net from distance at per-second rates, which is where most NHL attempts and blocks come from. Shot quality (0 to 1 from distance and angle, 75 ft horizon) still scales those volume rules. The slot and in-tight rules that used to decide close shots were replaced by xgChoice in sim 0.35.

perimeter.desc: A skater with a reasonable lane from the half wall, circles or point (28 to 55 ft) throws it at the net through traffic: that is where most NHL shots come from, and where most blocks happen.

breakaway.desc: An opponent counts as goal-side unless he is clearly behind the carrier (behindByFt); a wide opponent needs a bigger head start to be beaten.

xgChoice.desc: Shoot or pass, decided by the expected-goal model. Each tick in the offensive zone the carrier compares his own look (the model's xG from where he stands, times his finishing, times blockedLaneFactor if a defender is in the lane, times tightCoverFactor if a defender is within tightCoverFt of him: the model's xG assumes the usual NHL pressure, and a stick on the shooter takes most of a look away) with the best pass: a teammate's look (a one-timer if it goes cross-ice to an open man) times the chance the pass gets there (passCompleteBase minus passCompletePerFt per foot, at least passCompleteMin) and coveredFactor if a defender is within openFt of him. If his own look is at least minXg and within passMustBeatBy of the best pass, he shoots at shootRatePerSec scaled from 15% at minXg to full at cleanXg, and does not look for a discretionary pass unless a defender is within passUnderPressureFt. If a teammate's look is better by more than passMustBeatBy, he passes to him at passRatePerSec. Looks below minXg are left to the perimeter and point-shot rules.

dangerTiers.desc: Fallback only, used when the expected-goal model is not loaded. With the model, a shot's tier follows MoneyPuck's xG thresholds (low under 0.08, medium under 0.20, high 0.20 and up).

rulesBenchmarks.note: Approximate NHL per-team per-game rates. Icings: 10,264 icing events in the 2016-17 regular season (rjweise.github.io/Icing) over 1,230 games is about 8.3 per game, 4.2 per team. Offsides: roughly 6 per game league-wide from play-by-play stoppage counts, 3 per team.

sources.title: Looking at icing tendencies of NHL teams, players and coaches
Icing (ice hockey), Wikipedia: NHL hybrid icing rule

review.desc: The shot review after a Watch game. Every shot is judged by the carrier's own read at the moment he let it go, the same values his decisions and the sight lines use. A pass counts as a better option when it was worth passMustBeatBy times his shot (shotDecision.xgChoice) and at least minGapXg more; it is a close call when a pass was worth more but not by that much, and the right call otherwise. Each shot keeps leadSec of play before the release and afterSec after it, sampled sampleHz times a second, for the replay. Every snapshotEverySec of play it also keeps a snapshot of the whole game, so the what-if can rebuild the instant before any shot.

whatIf.desc: Play out the pass: the game is rebuilt on a separate engine at the instant before the shot, the shooter is made to pass to his best option instead, and the next horizonSec seconds (or until the whistle) are played runs times with fresh random numbers each time; the shot he took is played out the same number of times with the same random numbers, so each pair differs only by the choice. A choice is better when the 95% range of the paired difference in expected goals is above zero.

gapControl.desc: Gap control in the neutral zone: a defenseman keeps gapFt ahead of the deepest attacker, reading the attacker's speed readAheadSec ahead, so nobody gets behind him while the other team has the puck. In his own zone the zone coverage takes over.

angling.desc: On the entry and in the offensive zone, a defender who is goal-side of the puck carrier (at least goalSideFt closer to the net) and within engageFt of him, standing within laneFt of the carrier's route, takes away the inside: the carrier's route bends to the outside of him, wideFt past him toward the boards. Applies from fromFx (feet from the carrier's own end boards; the attacking blue line is at 114). Coaching references: a defenseman on the rush keeps the carrier to the outside and protects the middle.

crease.desc: The goal crease: a half circle radiusFt in front of each goal line. While his team has the puck, an attacker without it sets up at the edge of the other team's crease (setupFt from the middle of the goal line), screening from the top of the crease the way net-front forwards do, not standing in it; the carrier can skate through, and anyone can go in after a loose puck, as the rules allow. No skater, from either team, can stand on a goalie: within goalieRoomFt of him a skater is moved off, and the goalie keeps his spot. Rule 69 (goalie interference) takes away a goal when an attacker in the crease impairs the goalie, which these keep from happening.
